items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had also heard, although I hadn’t played with, Art Tatum

ctx.x: So there must have been something that . . .

Well, I had also heard, although I hadn’t played with, Art Tatum, and I felt at that time that Teddy Wilson was the closest thing to Art Tatum at that time, you know. Gee, I don’t know. He had the taste and the technique and the fluidity and the harmonic sensitivity; many things about his playing all . . .
And when you came back, I believe the next day, you were already in the studio with Teddy Wilson back in New York.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Tatum to me is almost like a sacred cow... I don't know -- it's very hard to criticize anything that he did.

ctx.x: I don't know. I guess it's almost like -- Tatum to me is almost like a sacred cow, I guess that's what -- what does that mean, like when I say a sacred cow, what does that mean?
